subject: Post-demo: data handling constraints & BYO key decision path
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sarah Bell <sarah.bell@medtechcorp.com>, Tom Keller <tom.keller@medtechcorp.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2028-04-03T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-demo: data handling constraints & BYO key decision path

Hi Sarah / Tom —

Thanks again for taking the demo this morning. Quick recap and suggested path forward so we can get your security team the artifacts they need. I summarized the key constraints you mentioned and next steps below.

Highlights from today
- PII scope: customer identifiers + device telemetry (low-cardinality) will be sent to Redwood-hosted endpoints for inference.
- Residency: production data must remain in US regions; EU test data will stay in eu-west.
- Retention: you need 30 days of request/response logs, plus a 90-day sampling window for audit sampling.
- Logging controls: must redact user-supplied PII in debug logs and provide an opt-in for verbose request traces.
- Encryption: TLS in transit mandatory; at-rest encryption with customer-managed keys preferred. You mentioned an HSM-backed KMS is a hard requirement for prod.

Suggested next steps (proposed timeline)
1) Risk/Q control pack — I attached a short BYO key overview + a runbook mapping (redwood-byo-overview.pdf). Will send SOC2 excerpts and a KMS/HSM evidence checklist. (EOD Thu)
2) Architecture sketch for restricted flows — model routing to a US-only private deployment with KV cache disabled for MR data. I can draft this in a 1-page diagram. (Monica to draft by Mon)
3) Deep-dive with security — schedule a 60-min technical session with your crypto/security folks to walk HSM integration and audit log access patterns. Aim for next Wed.
4) Procurement ask — Tom, if you can share any contract constraints around key custody and SLA credits we can align implementation and pricing.

Attachments: redwood-byo-overview.pdf (BYO key flows), runbook-kms-options.md (operational steps)

Happy to adjust — what should I prioritize for the security session?

Cheers,
Logan
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
log an.wright@redwoodinference.com | +1 415-555-0123

From: Sarah Bell <sarah.bell@medtechcorp.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Tom Keller <tom.keller@medtechcorp.com>
Date: 2028-04-03T12:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: data handling constraints & BYO key decision path

Thanks, Logan — great recap. A few clarifications from our side before we loop in security:  

1) HSM requirement: we operate with an existing AWS CloudHSM-backed KMS (customer account). We need Redwood to integrate with our KMS via an external key encryption (you rotate a CEK that you never persist) or accept wrapped keys pushed by us. Which of those are supported?
2) KV cache: your suggestion to disable for MR data sounds right. Will disabling impact latency SLAs for short burst traffic? If so we need a mitigation note.
3) Audit sampling: 90-day window is correct, but we will want a way to query unredacted request headers for a small scoped forensic process (approved people only). Do you support role-based access for raw traces?

I can free up our security lead for Wed afternoon PST. Please include your solutions/crypto engineer so we can run through the integration options.

Thanks,
Sarah
Security Ops Manager | MedTech Corp
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sarah Bell <sarah.bell@medtechcorp.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>, Tom Keller <tom.keller@medtechcorp.com>
Date: 2028-04-04T08:17:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: data handling constraints & BYO key decision path

Sarah — thanks, noted. Short answers and what we'll bring to the security deep-dive:  

1) KMS/HSM integration modes we support (we'll bring docs + runbook)
   - Wrapped-key push (you generate CEKs in your account, wrap with Redwood public key, we unwrap into an ephemeral in-memory CEK used for model loading; no persistent plaintext at rest).
   - External KMS RPC (Redwood delegates encryption operations to your KMS via customer-managed credentials and CloudHSM-backed key material; Redwood never exports key material).
   - HSM-backed vault on a private deployment (for mid-market we run a dedicated enclave that integrates with your HSM API; this is our recommended path for highest assurance).

2) KV cache impact
   - Disabling KV cache for MR path increases token-level latency by ~15-30% in our benchmarks for short sequences. Mitigations: prefix caching (retain non-PII prefixes) + pre-warm (predictive priming) to keep p50 within SLOs. We'll present numbers specific to your observed sequence lengths.

3) Audit & trace access
   - Yes: RBAC for trace access with fine-grained controls. Raw unredacted traces are stored in an encrypted object store with access gated by roles and audit logs; we can provide a short-lived export for forensic review scoped by query filters.

We'll prepare: architecture sketch, KMS integration decision matrix (security pros can pick wrapped-key vs delegated KMS), and an SLA note about latency impact and credits for KV-disabled flows. Proposed security deep-dive: Wed 2028-04-11 13:00 PST. Is that OK?

Attachments: (I attached the runbook-kms-options.md with code snippets and the public JWKS for wrapped-key uploads)

Best,
Logan
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sarah Bell <sarah.bell@medtechcorp.com>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>, Tom Keller <tom.keller@medtechcorp.com>
Date: 2028-04-05T14:33:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: data handling constraints & BYO key decision path

Sarah / team — looping in a brief procurement checklist so Tom can see the items we'll need to sign off technical and commercial:  

Procurement checklist (pre-contract)
- Confirm BYOK mode: Wrapped-key push OR delegated KMS (select one).
- Residency clause: prod in us-west-2 only; test in eu-west-1.
- Retention & logs: 30-day full logs + 90-day sampled traces; exportability clause for audits.
- SLA / credits: latency SLOs with KV-cache disabled (we'll include a service credit schedule if p50/p95 breach occurs due to this configuration).
- Evidence pack: SOC2 Type II excerpts, KMS integration whitepaper, HSM attestation options.

Tom — can you share any timing constraints for your procurement cycle? If we lock the BYOK mode now (wrapped-key push looks quickest), we can get a PoC running within 3 weeks with a limited private deployment for testing.

I'll draft the one-page architecture and the procurement checklist and send by EOD Friday.

Thanks,
Monica
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
